import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    events = inputs["events"].copy()
    
    # Sort by user_id, event_ts, event_id to ensure correct ordering
    events = events.sort_values(
        by=["user_id", "event_ts", "event_id"],
        na_position="last"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    # Calculate time gap from previous event (within same user)
    events["prev_event_ts"] = events.groupby("user_id")["event_ts"].shift(1)
    
    # Compute time delta in minutes
    events["time_gap_minutes"] = (
        events["event_ts"] - events["prev_event_ts"]
    ).dt.total_seconds() / 60
    
    # Determine if this is a new session:
    # - First event of a user (prev_event_ts is NaT) → new session
    # - Gap > 30 minutes → new session
    events["new_sess"] = (
        (events["prev_event_ts"].isna()) |
        (events["time_gap_minutes"] > 30)
    ).astype(int)
    
    # Cumulative sum to get session_num (1-based per user)
    events["session_num"] = events.groupby("user_id")["new_sess"].cumsum()
    
    # Group by user_id and session_num to aggregate
    user_sessions = events.groupby(
        ["user_id", "session_num"],
        as_index=False
    ).agg({
        "event_ts": ["min", "max"],
        "event_id": "count"
    })
    
    # Flatten column names
    user_sessions.columns = ["user_id", "session_num", "session_start", "session_end", "event_count"]
    
    # Ensure proper data types
    user_sessions["user_id"] = user_sessions["user_id"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["session_num"] = user_sessions["session_num"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["event_count"] = user_sessions["event_count"].astype("int64")
    user_sessions["session_start"] = pd.to_datetime(user_sessions["session_start"])
    user_sessions["session_end"] = pd.to_datetime(user_sessions["session_end"])
    
    return {"user_sessions": user_sessions}
